title: Alcohol Handoff, Returned Orders and Order Closing
content:
## Handoff operations standard — alcohol, returned orders and closing

This standard governs alcohol lines at handoff, orders that go back to the store, and the closing of a Cartwise Grocery Orders order.

### Alcohol

1. Alcohol lines are sold only on service levels on which alcohol is allowed, and are handed over only after a valid ID check.
2. When the ID check fails, the alcohol lines are refunded in full with the refund reason alcohol ID failed, and the service level's alcohol return fee is billed as an alcohol return fee.

### Returned orders

3. A delivery order is returned when the customer cannot be reached after the service level's number of contact attempts and its wait, in minutes, at the address. A pickup order is returned when it is not collected within its hold time.
4. On a returned order, the service level's returned-item refund percentage of the charge of each non-perishable line is refunded with the refund reason returned order. Perishable lines are not refunded.
5. Fees on a returned order are refunded only where the service level refunds fees on returned orders.

### Closing

6. A completed or returned order closes when its issue-report window ends.
7. A closed order takes no further item refund, tip change or fee refund.

### Returned-order lines (hypothetical figures)

For this illustration only, take a returned-item refund percentage of 40 on a returned order:

| Line | Item class | Line charge | Refunded as returned order |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper towels | Non-perishable | 10.00 | 4.00 |
| Strawberries | Perishable | 6.00 | Nothing |

### Points of judgement

- *Alcohol refused at the door because the ID check failed* — the alcohol lines come back in full and the alcohol return fee of the order's service level is billed (clause 2).
- *A customer asks for an item refund on an order that has closed* — a closed order takes no further item refund (clause 7).
- *A tip change asked for on a closed order* — not taken (clause 7).
